The core innovation of PIDO lies in its approach to learning shared latent representations of solutions, which are then used to model dynamics within a latent space. This is achieved through a combination of an auto-decoder to map solutions into a low-dimensional latent space and a neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) to model the temporal evolution within this latent space. The authors identify two key challenges in physics-informed loss: instability during training and degradation in time extrapolation. To address these issues, they propose two regularization techniques: latent dynamics smoothing and latent dynamics alignment. Latent dynamics smoothing aims to stabilize the latent space dynamics by penalizing rapid changes in the latent variables, while latent dynamics alignment ensures that the latent space representation is consistent across different time steps. The authors evaluate PIDO on a range of benchmark problems, including 1D and 2D combined equations and the Navier-Stokes equations, demonstrating improved performance compared to existing methods. The empirical results show that PIDO exhibits improved training stability and extrapolation performance, as well as enhanced transferability to downstream tasks such as long-term integration and inverse problems. The paper's main contribution is the novel approach of learning shared latent representations of PDE solutions, which allows the model to generalize better across different initial conditions, PDE coefficients, and training time horizons. This is achieved through a combination of physics-informed training in the latent space and the introduction of regularization techniques to improve training stability and extrapolation performance. The authors also demonstrate the transferability of the learned latent representations to downstream tasks, highlighting the robustness and adaptability of the proposed method. Overall, the paper presents a well-motivated and innovative approach to solving PDEs with deep learning, offering a promising alternative to traditional numerical methods.
